newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Bridge sees more revenue gains.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Bridge sees more revenue gains.

text.p: Chicago Bridge & Iron Co NV said it anticipates revenues to continue to increase over the next several quarters.

"The rate of revenue growth for 1997 is dependent on the amount and timing of new business taken during 1997 which will be executed during the current year," the engineering and construction firm said.

The company on Thursday reported net income of $3.1 million for the first quarter ended March 31, excluding the effect of a one-time, non-cash special charge of $16.7 million, or $10.1 million after tax.
Including the charge, the company had a net quarterly loss of $7 million compared to net income of $2.4 million for the first quarter of 1996.
Revenues for the most recent quarter were $150.4 million, up from from $139.7 million in the first quarter of 1996.
"The higher revenues are due to increased execution of work in South America, Asia, and the Middle East," CBI said.
Backlog at March 31 increased by $49.1 million to $534.8 million compared to a backlog of $485.7 million at December 31, 1996.

"New business taken during the quarter of $205.5 million remained strong, increasing slightly over $204.1 million taken in the same period of the prior year. As expected, approximately 60 percent of the new business taken during the quarter was for contracts outside of North America," CBI said.
